character_facts: Honorata is able to conceive despite Othon's inability to father a child normally.
Honorata protects Aghnar from Othon, raises him in exile, and trains him.
Othon is Aghnar's father and judges warrior worth through brutal tests.
Aghnar was born during a fall, is lighter than air because of epyphite, and eventually receives metal prosthetic feet.
Aghnar passes Othon's ordeal by defeating a robot and enduring the crushing of his feet without giving in.
characters_present: Several unidentified figures shown only as small portrait insets
continuity_links: This page is explicitly a recap of events before the current issue.
It connects Aghnar's childhood ordeal to the later Metabaron custom of ritual mutilation and prosthetic augmentation.
dialogue_meaning: The page contains no scene dialogue; it is a prose 'previously' recap summarizing prior story events.
The recap explains Aghnar's unusual birth, exile, training, ordeal, and the origin of prosthetic mutilation as a Metabaron rite.
lore_facts: A person can be impregnated in this setting using a drop of a warrior's blood.
An epyphite cartridge can make a falling person float on the wind.
Exposure to or introduction of epyphite during birth can make a child lighter than air.
Steel weights or bracelets can counteract Aghnar's weightlessness by keeping him on the ground.
Ansirma is described as a sacred mountain.
Metabaron initiation comes to include mutilation and prosthetic replacement.
The Shabda-Oud sought a hermaphrodite child as a political instrument to proclaim a perfect androgyne and seize the throne.
plot_events: A recap explains that Othon can no longer father a child, so Honorata impregnates herself using a drop of his blood.
Honorata's pregnancy proceeds until two jealous servants push or injure her at the top of the fortress.
As she falls, Othon fires an epyphite cartridge that lets her float on the wind, and she gives birth to Aghnar.
Honorata tells Othon that the Shabda-Oud expected a hermaphrodite child they could use to claim a perfect androgynous ruler and seize the throne.
Because epyphite was introduced during birth, Aghnar becomes lighter than air.
Othon wants to kill Aghnar because this condition means he cannot become a warrior, but Honorata prevents it.
Honorata fits Aghnar with steel bracelets at his waist and ankles to keep him grounded.
Honorata takes Aghnar into exile on the sacred mountain of Ansirma and trains his mental powers and pain resistance.
At age seven, Aghnar returns to the Castaka fortress for Othon's test.
Aghnar defeats a formidable robot as part of the test.
Aghnar endures a machine that crushes his feet without yielding, passes the test, and later receives metal prosthetic feet.
The recap states that mutilation and prostheses became part of Metabaron initiation from this event onward.
uncertainties: Some recap text is small and partially difficult to read; wording may be approximate even where the event sequence is clear.

The large illustrated woman is likely Honorata based on the recap context, but the image itself does not label her directly.
